name: FOXO4-DRI
lead: FOXO4-DRI is a research peptide designed to clear senescent ("zombie") cells, the aged cells that stop dividing and release inflammatory signals. It works by interrupting the interaction between FOXO4 and p53, which lets those cells undergo programmed death.[1][2] People interested in longevity and appearance follow it because senescent cells are linked to tissue ageing, including skin and fibroblast changes.

Its profile comes largely from a 2017 Cell paper in which a modified all-D-amino-acid peptide (the "DRI" stands for D-Retro-Inverso) restored p53 apoptosis in senescent cells and eased senescence-related loss of tissue function in mice.[1] Since then, laboratory and animal studies have looked at its effects in testis, lung, cartilage cells and keloid scar fibroblasts.[7][4][10][11] No human clinical trials have been published.

chain: Peptide blocks FOXO4-p53 binding in senescent cells
Fewer inflammatory senescent cells in tissue (shown in animals)
angle.text: Proponents discuss it as a way to clear aged cells that contribute to tissue ageing, which they connect to a younger-looking, healthier body. Published work so far is in cells and animals.

paras: In senescent cells FOXO4 binds p53 in the nucleus, which keeps p53 from triggering apoptosis. FOXO4-DRI competes with that binding, releasing p53 so the cell can die.[1] A 2025 structural study identified the disordered transactivation domain of p53 as the target of both FOXO4 and the peptide.[5]

No studies found. Related laboratory and animal research includes work in aged mice showing improved testosterone secretion and spermatogenesis through effects on senescent Leydig cells,[7][8] reduced fibrosis in a mouse lung model,[9] selective removal of senescent human chondrocytes in culture,[10] and induction of apoptosis in keloid senescent fibroblasts.[11]

A 2023 Circulation study found that eliminating senescent cells could promote pulmonary hypertension development in the models studied, indicating that clearing senescent cells can have context-dependent effects.[12] FOXO4-DRI is not an approved drug.

timeline.event: Baar and colleagues report FOXO4-DRI in Cell, showing it restored apoptosis in senescent cells and improved tissue function in aged mice.[1]
Study in aged mice links the peptide to improved testosterone secretion.[8]
Nature Communications paper maps the p53 domain targeted by FOXO4 and FOXO4-DRI.[5]

card.summary: A senolytic research peptide that clears aged senescent cells, followed by longevity-minded people for its potential effect on tissue ageing.
card.note: Research compound with animal and cell data only; no published human trials.

quick.overview:
FOXO4-DRI is a peptide that blocks the FOXO4-p53 interaction so senescent cells can die. It is discussed in longevity circles as a way to reduce the inflammatory burden of aged cells.

Published work consists of cell and mouse studies, including testis, lung, cartilage cells and keloid fibroblasts.
quick.mechanism: In senescent cells FOXO4 holds p53 in the nucleus and prevents apoptosis; the D-retro-inverso peptide disrupts that binding, releasing p53 to trigger cell death.
quick.risks: It is not an approved drug and has no published human trials. A 2023 study reported that removing senescent cells could worsen pulmonary hypertension in the models used.
